subject: maths
note: Applied to every worked solution and to feedback. 'marker' names the deterministic check the marking engine can run; 'coach' is the sentence shown to the learner. All wording is ours; sources are the CCEA General Marking Advice (Summer 2025 M4 MS), the paper front-page instructions, and the Chief Examiner reports as summarised in docs/research/01 (§9, parallel version §11.5).

rules.rule: Write the final answer on the answer line, and make sure it is the answer from the method you trust.
rules.why: Several answers with nothing on the answer line means the poorest one is marked; several methods means only the one leading to the answer-line answer is marked.
rules.coach: Put one answer on the line — the marker follows that answer back to its method.
rules.source: CCEA General Marking Advice (v), Summer 2025 M4 MS; CER November 2025 (docs/sources/maths/report-november2025-plain.txt line 366: multiple solutions with no answer on the line — the worst is marked)

rules.rule: If you start again, cross out the attempt you are abandoning; never leave two competing solutions.
rules.why: Crossed-out work that has not been replaced is still marked, and two answers left standing are marked at the poorer one.
rules.coach: One clear attempt scores better than two half-finished ones.
rules.source: CCEA General Marking Advice (iv), (v), Summer 2025 M4 MS; research 01 (parallel) §11.5

rules.rule: Keep full calculator accuracy in the working and round only at the end; if the question states an accuracy, give exactly that.
rules.why: The scheme credits the most accurate figure seen unless a particular accuracy is demanded; rounding part-way (e.g. a trig value) loses the accuracy mark.
rules.coach: Write the long version, then round on the answer line.
rules.source: CCEA General Marking Advice (viii), Summer 2025 M4 MS; CER Summer 2025 M3 general comment on rounding and accuracy (docs/sources/maths/report-summer2025-plain.txt line 348); research 01 (parallel) §11.5

rules.rule: Obey a stated accuracy ('to 1 decimal place', 'to 3 significant figures', 'to the nearest degree') exactly — no more places, no fewer.
rules.why: The final accuracy mark is tied to the demanded form; 'appropriate degree of accuracy' means no more places than the data given.
rules.coach: Underline the accuracy words before you start.
rules.source: Paper instruction phrases counted in the corpus ("give your answer to 1 decimal place" 13, "to 3 significant figures", "to the nearest degree"); CCEA Teacher Guidance 2019 on 'appropriate degree of accuracy' (research 01 §4); CER November 2025 Q25 (rounding 1.347… to 1.35)

rules.rule: Give units where none are printed on the answer line, and give money to two decimal places (or in pence if the question says pence).
rules.why: 'pence' in bold was ignored by most candidates and cost the mark; money answers such as £96.2 lose the accuracy mark.
rules.coach: £ answers end in two digits; pence answers have no £.
rules.source: CER Summer 2025 M2 Q18 (docs/sources/maths/report-summer2025-plain.txt line 254: 'pence' in bold ignored); research 01 (parallel) §11.5; concept C §6.9

rules.rule: Write probabilities as fractions, decimals or percentages — never as ratios or words.
rules.why: Ratio notation and word answers score nothing for a probability.
rules.coach: 3/8, 0.375 or 37.5% — not 3:8 and not 'unlikely'.
rules.source: research 01 (parallel) §11.5 (examiner comments on ratio notation and word answers for probabilities); concept C §6.9

rules.rule: On a calculator paper, still write the calculation you keyed in before the result.
rules.why: A wrong answer with no working scores zero; the written calculation earns the method mark even when the number is wrong.
rules.coach: One line of working is your insurance policy.
rules.source: Paper front page: 'All working must be clearly shown ... Marks may be awarded for partially correct solutions' (M4 Summer 2025); research 01 (parallel) §11.5 (calculator inputs not shown); CER Summer 2025 M5 P2 general comment (working shown on a calculator paper)

rules.rule: Bold words in the stem are instructions the marker enforces: estimate, form an equation, use a scale drawing, single transformation, in pence, do not measure, without a calculator.
rules.why: Ignoring a bold instruction usually zeroes the part even when the maths is right.
rules.coach: Read the bold twice.
rules.source: research 01 (parallel) §11.5; corpus phrase counts (estimate 250, single transformation 40, form an equation 4, use a scale drawing 2, without using a calculator 2); CER Summer 2025 M2 Q18

rules.rule: When told to estimate, round each number to one significant figure first, then calculate; an exact calculation scores nothing.
rules.why: The marks are for the rounding and the approximate calculation, not for the exact answer.
rules.coach: Estimate = round, then work.
rules.source: CER Summer 2025 M5 P1 Q3 (docs/sources/maths/report-summer2025-plain.txt line 445: candidates who ignore the instruction to estimate); concept C §6.1

rules.rule: Where a question says form an equation, or the topic is solving/simultaneous equations, use an algebraic method; trial and improvement earns no method marks.
rules.why: Method marks are attached to the algebraic steps.
rules.coach: Trial and improvement can find the number but not the marks.
rules.source: research 01 (parallel) §11.5; CER Summer 2025 M2 Q26 (trial and improvement used for equations, docs/sources/maths/report-summer2025-plain.txt line 189)

rules.rule: 'Describe fully' a transformation means every detail: reflection — the line; rotation — centre, angle and direction; translation — the vector; enlargement — centre and scale factor. One transformation only when the stem says single.
rules.why: Each missing detail loses a mark; two transformations for a 'single transformation' scores zero.
rules.coach: Name it, then give every number it needs.
rules.source: corpus phrase counts (describe fully 40, single transformation 40); research 01 §9.4 (only one candidate gained both marks); concept C §6.1

rules.rule: Constructions are done with ruler and compasses in dark pencil, and the construction arcs are left visible.
rules.why: The arcs are the evidence of method; papers are scanned, so faint pencil disappears.
rules.coach: Arcs are marks — do not rub them out.
rules.source: M8 Paper 1 Summer 2025 Q2 instruction not to rub out construction arcs (docs/sources/maths/past-papers/summer2025-M8-paper1-noncalc-front.txt); paper front page: drawing in HB pencil; research 01 (parallel) §11.5 (freehand lines, scanned scripts)

rules.rule: Digits must be unambiguous (1 vs 7, 0 vs 6); use black ink for writing and HB pencil for drawing; stay inside the boxed area.
rules.why: Scripts are scanned; illegible digits are marked as read. Gel pen and work outside the box may not be captured.
rules.coach: If a 7 could be a 1, it is a 1.
rules.source: Paper front-page instructions (black ink, no gel pen, HB pencil, boxed area — M4 Summer 2025); CER November 2025 (docs/sources/maths/report-november2025-plain.txt line 215: increasing number of responses very difficult to read)

rules.rule: Use brackets when substituting negative numbers and when multiplying out; write (−3)² not −3².
rules.why: Missing brackets is a recurring cause of lost accuracy marks in algebra.
rules.coach: Brackets around every negative you substitute.
rules.source: CER Summer 2025 M3 general comment (docs/sources/maths/report-summer2025-plain.txt line 348: use of brackets in algebra was an issue); scheme phrase 'brackets' 155 occurrences

rules.rule: Keep the inequality sign through the solution and in the final answer; reverse it when multiplying or dividing by a negative.
rules.why: An inequality solved as an equation loses the final mark.
rules.coach: x > 4, not x = 4.
rules.source: concept C §6.9; research 01 §9 (inequality answers given as equations)

rules.rule: Write a product of prime factors with × signs and index notation, e.g. 2³ × 3 × 5.
rules.why: A list of factors is not a product; recognising squares from the index form is examined.
rules.coach: Multiply signs and powers.
rules.source: concept C §6.9; CER November 2025 M6 Q26 (docs/sources/maths/report-november2025-plain.txt line 248: square numbers written as products of primes)

rules.rule: Check the answer against the context: a probability is at most 1, an estimated mean lies inside the data range, an estimate sits below the population size, a length is positive.
rules.why: Impossible answers signal a method error the marker cannot follow through.
rules.coach: Does the number make sense? If not, look for the slip.
rules.source: concept C §6.9; research 01 §9.3–9.4 general advice

rules.rule: Set the calculator to give decimal answers (not fractions or surds) and know the order-of-operations keys; bring a calculator to calculator papers.
rules.why: Examiners report candidates sitting calculator papers without one, or copying fraction displays instead of decimals.
rules.coach: Check the display mode the night before.
rules.source: CER Summer 2024 M2 Q17 (docs/sources/maths/report-summer2024-plain.txt lines 153-159: no calculator; wrong mode); research 01 (parallel) §5

rules.rule: On Paper 1 of a completion test, show a written method (column methods, fraction work, surd manipulation) — numbers are chosen to be done by hand.
rules.why: Paper 1 is marked on the written method; an unsupported answer earns the accuracy mark only if the method is visible.
rules.coach: Show the arithmetic you would have typed.
rules.source: Specification §4.6 (calculators must not be used in Paper 1 of each completion test; docs/sources/maths/spec-2017-current_0.txt lines 1328-1330); M8 Paper 1 front page

rules.rule: In bounds questions write the full calculator display before rounding, and use the correct half-unit (e.g. 47.5 for 50 kg to the nearest 5 kg).
rules.why: The upper/lower bound marks depend on the exact bound and the unrounded result.
rules.coach: Half the rounding unit, both ways.
rules.source: CER Summer 2025 M4 Q13 (docs/sources/maths/report-summer2025-plain.txt line 386); concept C §6.9

rules.rule: When asked for a reason, use the mathematical words tied to the data ('the range is affected by the extreme value 98'); a label such as 'Z angles' or 'alternate' alone is not a reason.
rules.why: Reason marks need the property named in full and applied to the figures.
rules.coach: Name the rule and point at the numbers.
rules.source: research 01 §9.3–9.4 (reasons given as labels); concept C §6.1

rules.rule: Convert to consistent units before calculating and state the unit of the answer (metric conversions must be known: 1 kg = 1000 g, 1 litre = 1000 cm³, 1 cm = 10 mm; 5 miles ≈ 8 km).
rules.why: Unit errors lose the accuracy mark and are reported every series at Foundation.
rules.coach: Same units in, one unit out.
rules.source: CER November 2025 M1 Q6 and Q14 (docs/sources/maths/report-november2025-plain.txt lines 121, 135, 222); research 01 §4 (conversions to be known)
